basis: The firm's own post of 2006-10-18: 'Benchmark Capital Europe leads €12.5 million investment in Igglo, the online estate agent' ('Igglo Oy, the Finnish online estate agency, today announces that it has raised €12.5m in funding led by Benchmark Capital Europe, the top-tie...'). Not on the desk pages or any later list; the company went bankrupt in February 2008.

The firm's own post of 2007-01-30: 'WHISHER Receives Funding from Benchmark Capital Europe and Swisscom' ('WHISHER, a Spanish company launching the first social network powered by a Wi-Fi network, today announced it has received investment f...'). Not on the desk pages or any later list.

The firm carried the announcement in its own news archive (2007-05-14: 'Power Challenge offers 3D sports games from your browser'); TechCrunch of 2007-05-14: 'Swedish Game Site Power Challenge Raises $8 Million From Benchmark Capital'. The London desk made the investment; not on any later list. Bought by Stillfront in November 2012.

The firm carried a feature on the company in its own news archive (2008-01-28: 'Zubka and the referral boom - Is Web 2.0 just the job?'); Startups.co.uk's 2008 list records that Zubka secured venture backing from Balderton, previously Benchmark. Job referral site, closed in December 2010; not on any later list.

note: Finnish online estate agent (Igglo Oy, founded February 2006); EUR 12.5M 'first venture round' led by Benchmark Capital Europe, October 2006 (the firm's own post), which names no series; bankrupt in February 2008, brokerage closed and the website sold to Sanoma (Inman)
Wi-Fi sharing network; investment from Benchmark Capital Europe and Swisscom, January 2007 (the firm's own post), amount and round not given; the company's later fate is on vendor pages only
Browser football games (Power Challenge, ManagerZone); $8M from Benchmark Capital's London desk, May 2007 (TechCrunch; the firm's own archive), round not named; acq. by Stillfront, November 2012

Job referral site paying users for recommendations; venture backing from Balderton (Startups.co.uk 2008; a feature in the firm's own archive, January 2008), round not on a citable surface; closed in December 2010
